question.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & -4 \\ -4 & 2 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & -2 & -1 & 3 \\ 7 & -1 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{13}$ equal to zero.*
question.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{13}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & -4 \\ -4 & 2 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & -2 & -1 & 3 \\ 7 & -1 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+(-1){C}_{3} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+(-3){C}_{3} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+4{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -6 & -4 & 2 & 9 \\ 6 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 9 & 5 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $1$st row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -6 & -4 & 2 & 9 \\ 6 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 9 & 5 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{1+3}|\begin{aligned}-6 & -4 & 9 \\ 6 & 1 & -1 \\ 9 & 5 & -6\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-6 & -4 & 9 \\ 6 & 1 & -1 \\ 9 & 5 & -6\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
